claims.title: Inference request flooding exhausts GPU-backed serving capacity
claims.description: A calling team holding an issued API key can send inexpensive requests from `entity:calling-service` across `flow:calling-service-to-inference-gateway:submit-inference-request` to the internet-facing `process:inference-gateway`. Each accepted request is forwarded over `flow:inference-gateway-to-model-server:forward-request` to `process:model-server` for GPU inference, making attacker request volume cheaper than the GPU, gateway-worker, feature-read, and logging work imposed on the service. Capacity limits, request-size limits, and load shedding are not represented in the model. Second-order, saturation of the availability-critical model server prevents inference for all calling services and continues to drive reads to `store:feature-store` and writes to `store:inference-log` until the serving path sheds load.

grounds.text: The gateway forwards the request to the model server, which runs the actual model on GPU nodes
Callers pass an API key in a header. Keys are issued per calling team and we have never expired one.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium: `flow:calling-service-to-inference-gateway:submit-inference-request` crosses from `boundary:public-internet`, but the attacker must hold a per-team API key; the stated non-expiring keys make that prerequisite persistent. Impact is high because both `process:inference-gateway` and `process:model-server` are tagged `availability-critical`, and every inference caller depends on the forwarded GPU-serving path.

mitigations.summary: Apply identity-bound request and cost limits before forwarding inference
mitigations.detail: At `process:inference-gateway`, enforce per-team rate, concurrency, token/input-size, and inference-cost budgets before sending work on `flow:inference-gateway-to-model-server:forward-request`.

mitigations.summary: Bound downstream work and shed overload
mitigations.detail: Use bounded gateway and model-server queues, request deadlines, concurrency caps, and fail-fast load shedding so a burst cannot indefinitely consume GPU workers or propagate work to `store:feature-store` and `store:inference-log`.

mitigations.summary: Rotate and scope caller API keys
mitigations.detail: Expire and rotate the per-team keys used on `flow:calling-service-to-inference-gateway:submit-inference-request`, allowing rate budgets and revocation to be applied to a verified caller identity.

claims.title: A publisher who substitutes an unverified model artifact can inherit the model server's authority
claims.description: If the unknown publication authentication on `flow:ml-engineer-to-model-registry:publish-artifact` permits a compromised or improperly shared publisher identity to write an attacker-controlled artifact, that actor can plant it in `store:model-registry`. `process:model-server` loads registry artifacts without integrity verification through `flow:model-server-to-model-registry:load-artifact`; if the artifact format or loader executes supplied logic, that logic runs with the model server's authority. The attacker thereby escalates from artifact-publication authority to the model server's model-network position and can use its unauthenticated read path on `flow:model-server-to-feature-store:read-features` to reach the confidential per-customer financial and PII features in `store:feature-store`. This is conditional on resolving the publisher authentication and on whether the artifact loader can execute attacker-controlled logic.

grounds.text: I don't believe anything verifies the artifact hasn't been swapped — we just trust the bucket.
Redis has no password on it; it is only reachable inside the model network.

verdict.reason: The claim rests on `authentication` on `flow:ml-engineer-to-model-registry:publish-artifact`, which the input never stated.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional because authentication on `flow:ml-engineer-to-model-registry:publish-artifact` is unknown, while a substituted artifact is explicitly not integrity-verified before loading. Impact is high because code running as `process:model-server` can reach `store:feature-store`, which is confidential and tagged `pii` and `financial`, over the unauthenticated `flow:model-server-to-feature-store:read-features`.

mitigations.summary: Require authenticated, attributable artifact publication and verified artifacts
mitigations.detail: Replace the unknown or potentially shared publication identity on `flow:ml-engineer-to-model-registry:publish-artifact` with individual or workload identities, limit writers, and require signed artifacts whose signature and provenance are verified by `process:model-server` before loading.

mitigations.summary: Isolate artifact execution from model-server authority
mitigations.detail: Load supplied artifacts in a sandboxed, minimally privileged execution environment with no ambient feature-store access; grant any required artifact-loading identity only read access to the specific approved artifact.

claims.title: Unverified internet transport could expose inference requests and long-lived API keys
claims.description: `flow:calling-service-to-inference-gateway:submit-inference-request` crosses from `boundary:public-internet` to `process:inference-gateway` and carries end-user text, but its `encryption_in_transit` value is unknown despite using HTTPS. If transport protection is not enforced end-to-end, an on-path attacker between the calling service and gateway can intercept request PII and the per-team API key sent in the header. The disclosed non-expiring key can then be used to reach `process:inference-gateway` as that calling team, enabling subsequent attacks against the inference API.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on the unknown transport setting: the flow crosses from `boundary:public-internet`, making on-path observation plausible, but an attacker must obtain a network position. Impact is high because the flow carries `pii` and interception can also disclose a never-expiring API key that reaches `process:inference-gateway`.

mitigations.summary: Verify and enforce TLS for the public inference flow
mitigations.detail: Require TLS 1.2+ with certificate validation for `flow:calling-service-to-inference-gateway:submit-inference-request`, and record the verified `encryption_in_transit` posture.

mitigations.summary: Replace static team API keys
mitigations.detail: Use short-lived, rotatable workload credentials so an intercepted credential does not provide durable access to the gateway.

claims.title: A storage-layer copy could disclose all feature-store customer data if encryption at rest is absent
claims.description: `store:feature-store` is classified confidential and contains PII and financial customer features, while its `encryption_at_rest` attribute is unknown. If that unknown resolves to unencrypted storage, an attacker who obtains the Redis storage media or an operational copy such as a snapshot can read account-age and spend-band records without authenticating through `process:model-server`. The resulting corpus can be correlated with inference activity to profile or target customers. This threat is conditional on the unverified at-rest encryption state, not an assertion that encryption is absent.

verdict.reason: The claim rests on `encryption_at_rest` on `store:feature-store`, which the input never stated.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on `unknown:store:feature-store:encryption_at_rest`: obtaining a storage-layer copy requires access beyond the normal application path, but no verified at-rest control is stated. Impact is high because the confidential store is tagged `pii` and `financial` and a copied dataset can expose many customers at once.

mitigations.summary: Verify and enforce encryption at rest for feature data and operational copies
mitigations.detail: Establish the `store:feature-store` encryption posture, then use managed encryption keys for its persisted data and explicitly protect snapshots, backups, and replicas with equivalent controls.

mitigations.summary: Restrict storage-layer and export access
mitigations.detail: Limit who can create, restore, export, or mount feature-store operational copies, and audit those actions.

claims.title: Raw prompts retained in the inference log could be disclosed from unverified storage copies
claims.description: `process:inference-gateway` writes every request and response, including raw end-user prompts, to confidential `store:inference-log`. Its `encryption_at_rest` setting is unknown. If the log storage or an operational copy is not encrypted at rest, a person who obtains storage-layer access can read accumulated prompts without using the gateway's API-key path. Because `flow:inference-gateway-to-inference-log:write-request-log` continuously adds request content, the exposure grows over time and can reveal PII and sensitive context usable in later social-engineering or account-targeting attacks. This threat is conditional on the unresolved at-rest encryption attribute.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt and tightly control inference-log storage copies

claims.title: A model engineer may deny publishing a model artifact because publication identity is not individually attributable
claims.description: `entity:ml-engineer` publishes artifacts through `flow:ml-engineer-to-model-registry:publish-artifact` into `store:model-registry`, but that flow's `authentication` is unknown and the submitted description says it may use a shared group account. If publication events identify only that group credential, any engineer authorized to use it can plausibly deny publishing a disputed artifact because the evidence identifies a population rather than an individual. This is conditional on resolving the unknown authentication and on what identity any publication record retains; it is not an assertion that no audit record exists. Second-order: `process:model-server` loads artifacts from `store:model-registry` at startup, so an unattributable artifact publication can leave the team unable to establish responsibility for model behavior across inference workloads.

Impact is high because `store:model-registry` holds `business-critical-data` and its artifacts are loaded by `process:model-server`, making attribution failure relevant to model behavior across serving workloads.

claims.title: A compromised artifact publisher can plant an unverified model
claims.description: `store:model-registry` holds artifacts that `process:model-server` loads at startup without integrity verification. If the unknown authentication on `flow:ml-engineer-to-model-registry:publish-artifact` permits an unauthorized or improperly shared publisher identity, an attacker can plant a modified model artifact in `store:model-registry`. On the next startup, `process:model-server` loads the planted artifact as trusted model data; the integrity loss therefore changes the behavior of every inference consumer rather than only one stored object. This threat is conditional on the unresolved publisher-authentication control, while the lack of artifact verification is explicitly described.

claims.title: Unverified model artifacts can disable inference during model-server startup

Authentication for the engineer-to-registry write flow is unknown, and the submitted description states that the model server performs no artifact-integrity verification; therefore this threat is conditional on an attacker obtaining that write path, including through the suspected shared publishing account. Second-order, disabling the availability-critical `process:model-server` removes the destination of `flow:inference-gateway-to-model-server:forward-request`, causing the internet-facing gateway's legitimate inference requests to fail regardless of its own remaining capacity.

mitigations.summary: Prevent a bad release from sustaining an outage
mitigations.detail: Keep a validated last-known-good artifact and isolate startup/load failures so `process:model-server` can roll back rather than crash-looping on the same registry object.

claims.title: A foothold in the internet-facing gateway reaches the unauthenticated model-network inference surface
claims.description: An attacker who obtains a foothold in `process:inference-gateway` inherits its network position and can invoke `process:model-server` through `flow:inference-gateway-to-model-server:forward-request`, which crosses from `boundary:serving-edge` into `boundary:model-network` but has no authentication. This turns compromise of the internet-facing gateway into access to the internal inference surface as the trusted gateway, rather than requiring the attacker to hold a model-network identity. The terminal capability is arbitrary submission of requests to `process:model-server` from the gateway's trusted position; authorization of those requests must therefore be enforced by the receiving process, not by network reachability alone.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium because `process:inference-gateway` is internet-facing and the crossing on `flow:inference-gateway-to-model-server:forward-request` accepts no authentication, although exploitation requires a foothold in the gateway. Impact is medium because the crossing grants access to the internal `process:model-server`, which handles business-critical inference workloads.

mitigations.summary: Authenticate and authorize the gateway-to-model-server hop
mitigations.detail: Require `process:model-server` to verify a workload identity from `process:inference-gateway` on `flow:inference-gateway-to-model-server:forward-request` and authorize the forwarded caller or tenant per request.

mitigations.summary: Restrict model-network ingress to a narrowly scoped gateway identity
mitigations.detail: Use network policy and short-lived workload credentials so only the intended gateway workload can reach the model-server interface, while retaining receiving-side authentication as the authorization boundary.

claims.title: Unverified gateway-to-model-server transport could expose customer inference payloads
claims.description: `flow:inference-gateway-to-model-server:forward-request` crosses from `boundary:serving-edge` into `boundary:model-network`, carries inference request payloads, and has both an unknown protocol and `encryption_in_transit` value. If this internal hop is not encrypted, a compromised workload or network observer on that path can intercept customer request content sent by `process:inference-gateway` to `process:model-server`. The captured request context can be correlated with the feature reads that `process:model-server` performs from `store:feature-store`, improving later targeting of customer data.

verdict.reason: The claim rests on `protocol` on `flow:inference-gateway-to-model-server:forward-request`, `encryption_in_transit` on `flow:inference-gateway-to-model-server:forward-request`, which the input never stated.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium and conditional on the unknown transport posture: the flow crosses into `boundary:model-network`, though the attacker needs an on-path foothold. Impact is medium because the flow is tagged `pii` and exposes customer inference-request payloads.

mitigations.summary: Encrypt and mutually authenticate the internal inference hop
mitigations.detail: Use mTLS between `process:inference-gateway` and `process:model-server`, set an explicit protocol, and record `encryption_in_transit` as verified.

claims.title: A stolen long-lived team API key lets an attacker submit inference as that team
claims.description: An attacker who obtains a per-team API key can present it over `flow:calling-service-to-inference-gateway:submit-inference-request` from the public internet and be accepted by `process:inference-gateway` as `entity:calling-service`. Because the key never expires or rotates, replay remains possible until it is manually replaced. Second-order, the impersonated caller can cause requests containing end-user text to be forwarded on `flow:inference-gateway-to-model-server:forward-request` into `process:model-server`, which reads customer features and supports the inference service.

mitigations.detail: Use workload identity federation or short-lived OAuth/OIDC access tokens on `flow:calling-service-to-inference-gateway:submit-inference-request`, bound to `process:inference-gateway` and the calling team.

mitigations.summary: Rotate and scope any remaining API keys
mitigations.detail: Set expiry and rotation requirements, issue a distinct key per workload rather than only per team, and monitor key use for unexpected source locations or request patterns.

claims.title: Network-position trust lets a serving-edge attacker impersonate the inference gateway
claims.description: An attacker who gains a foothold in `boundary:serving-edge` can send fabricated requests on `flow:inference-gateway-to-model-server:forward-request` and be treated by `process:model-server` as `process:inference-gateway`, because authentication is explicitly absent and acceptance relies on network position. Second-order, the forged request reaches the model server's inference path, including its reads of customer features from `store:feature-store` and its use of model artifacts from `store:model-registry`; the attacker's reach is therefore not limited to the network edge.

claims.title: Unauthenticated Redis access lets a model-network foothold pose as the model server
claims.description: An attacker with a foothold in `boundary:model-network` can connect through `flow:model-server-to-feature-store:read-features` and be accepted by `store:feature-store` as a trusted `process:model-server` caller because the flow's authentication is explicitly absent. This is identity trust by network position rather than verified workload identity. Second-order, the impostor can request the per-customer account-age and spend-band data held in the confidential feature store, rather than being limited to the permissions of its original compromised neighbor.

claims.title: An internal attacker can alter customer features in the passwordless Redis store
claims.description: `store:feature-store` is accessed over `flow:model-server-to-feature-store:read-features` with `authentication: none`, and the system description states that Redis has no password. An attacker who gains access to `boundary:model-network` can directly alter account-age or spend-band records in `store:feature-store` without presenting a store credential. Second-order, `process:model-server` reads those manipulated per-customer features for inference requests, so corrupted data can change model inputs and resulting decisions for affected customers.

rejected_claims.title: Unauthenticated model-server requests can be forged from the serving edge
rejected_claims.description: `flow:inference-gateway-to-model-server:forward-request` crosses from `boundary:serving-edge` into `boundary:model-network` but has `authentication: none`. An attacker with a foothold in the serving edge, or otherwise able to reach that internal path, can send fabricated inference requests directly to `process:model-server`; the model server has no stated caller check to distinguish those requests from ones forwarded by `process:inference-gateway`. The forged payload is processed as legitimate inference work, allowing attacker-chosen inputs to alter outputs returned through the normal request path.

grounds.text: There is no auth between the gateway and the model server; the model network is meant to be reachable only from the gateway.

verdict.reason: This is a spoofing threat: fabricated requests are accepted as though sent by `process:inference-gateway`, while attacker-chosen inference input producing its normal output does not identify unauthorized modification of data, code, configuration, or persisted component state.

severity.justification: Likelihood is medium because the absent authentication on `flow:inference-gateway-to-model-server:forward-request` makes forgery possible after a serving-edge or network-path foothold, but that foothold is still required. Impact is medium because fabricated inputs are accepted by `process:model-server`, which holds `business-critical-data` and supports an availability-critical inference service.

mitigations.summary: Authenticate the gateway-to-model-server flow
mitigations.detail: Require mTLS or workload-identity authentication on `flow:inference-gateway-to-model-server:forward-request`, and configure `process:model-server` to reject callers other than the authorized inference gateway identity.

mitigations.summary: Validate forwarded request provenance
mitigations.detail: Have `process:inference-gateway` sign or attach authenticated claims to forwarded requests and have `process:model-server` verify them before running inference.
